_comment: How gales come over an Age (Jonah, 2026-11-04, notes/wind-plan.md): `often` is how much of the time one
blows, `push` how hard it leans, and `gusts`, `force` and `sudden` how often it gusts, how hard a gust
shoves, and how little warning one gives.
Mild until its gusts: a steady lean is at worst a nuisance, so `often` and the first steps of `push` are
strange, and a short book's gale only leans. A gust can throw you off a ledge, so the gust dials are
harmful, climbing to failing at the top. Only where there is a sky for it to blow under.
